title_ru: Fallout 3 — датамайнинг скрытого и осиротевшего контента F3DAD
title_en: Fallout 3 — F3DAD Hidden & Orphaned Content Datamining Registry

purpose.ru: Зафиксировать предметы и механики Fallout 3, обнаруженные через анализ официальных ESM из пользовательского архива F3DAD.rar, с приоритетом на формы без штатного runtime-пути, тестовые ревизии, orphan-записи и функциональные цепочки WEAP/MISC -> ENCH/MGEF -> SCPT/PROJ/EXPL.
purpose.en: Preserve hidden, test, revision and orphaned Fallout 3 records reconstructed directly from the official ESM graph, while separating primary-byte observations from interpretation and from claims about public novelty.

source_lineage.scope_note: This artifact does not claim new SHA-256 values for DLC ESM files unless independently recomputed; the outer archive receipt is the lineage anchor for the six-master set.

primary_questions: Does the record exist in a shipped official master?
Does it have a normal world, container, NPC, quest or script acquisition/use path?
If it is unplaced, does a functional effect/script/projectile chain still survive?
Does an apparently unused form preserve a prior revision of a production mechanic?
Are two records structurally identical except for identity/editor metadata?
Is the finding merely a known cut item, or does the ESM graph expose additional undocumented structure?

evidence_layers.L0_PRIMARY_BYTES: The form/subrecord/script exists in one of the official ESM files contained in the registered F3DAD archive.
evidence_layers.L1_REFERENCE_GRAPH: Inbound and outbound relations among forms are reconstructed from the ESM records.
evidence_layers.L2_SCRIPT_SEMANTICS: Compiled/decompiled script behavior is interpreted only where the relevant form/script relationship is present.
evidence_layers.L3_RUNTIME_REACHABILITY: Normal acquisition/use is distinguished from zero-reference or test-cell-only reachability.
evidence_layers.L4_PUBLIC_FOOTPRINT: Public mention of a name or EditorID is treated separately from primary-asset graph reconstruction.
evidence_layers.L5_INTERPRETATION: Development intent or revision history remains an inference unless explicitly stated by a primary artifact.

terminology.orphan_record: A record present in the shipped master with no observed normal inbound runtime path in the inspected graph.
terminology.hidden_mechanic: A surviving functional chain whose behavior is not represented by a normally obtainable production item.
terminology.revision_ghost: A record that appears to preserve an abandoned or superseded implementation revision.
terminology.test_cell_asset: A valid inventory/object form retained in developer/test content rather than the normal game path.

form_id_notation.note: xx is the runtime load-order byte and is installation dependent.

primary_observation.mechanic: Successive hits against the same target advance an internal damage level; changing target resets the sequence.
reconstructed_incremental_damage_sequenc: second same-target hit: +5 direct HP damage
third same-target hit: +10 direct HP damage
fourth and later same-target hits: +20 direct HP damage per hit

findings.interpretation: Bethesda retained a test implementation of focus-fire damage escalation for an electric sword. The strongest claim is the surviving stateful same-target mechanic, not novelty of the EditorID itself.

paired_test_record.observed_role: Test/controller weapon associated with bombFlareActive state.

findings.script_behavior_summary: The surviving effect chain places DLC02FXCarpetBomb01 objects during the scripted effect lifecycle. A related level-design prototype also retains a short delayed call-in flow.
findings.interpretation: The records collectively preserve an abandoned player-triggered flare/call-in path for carpet bombing rather than a mere inert weapon model.

findings.orphan_gap_signature: 01 -> base, 02 -> 02, 03 -> 04; helper WEAP 03 survives but is skipped by the observed VTwo dispatch chain.
findings.interpretation: The skipped 03 helper is consistent with a superseded intermediate implementation or renumbered Tesla chain stage.

findings.primary_observation: B and C were observed as structurally identical across the compared gameplay/model/audio/projectile-related subrecords, with EditorID identity as the meaningful distinction, and neither had a normal observed runtime use path.
findings.interpretation: B and C are strong candidates for abandoned revision copies of the non-player Robot Cannon implementation.

observations: These are MISC inventory forms rather than only STATIC scenery records.
They are associated with developer/test content rather than ordinary player-facing placement.
The EditorID DLC05AlienThingamabon preserves the apparent terminal-n spelling in the shipped data.
findings.interpretation: The set preserves a developer-facing alien-junk vocabulary and inventory-object family that did not become a normal collectible set in the released player path.

novelty_policy.admitted_claim: This registry preserves primary-asset graph reconstructions and hidden mechanics recovered from the registered ESM set.
novelty_policy.forbidden_claim_without_broader_archive_: No person or website has ever documented any of these records or mechanics.
novelty_policy.reason: Historical modding forums, dumps, mirrors and non-indexed archives make universal public-novelty claims non-falsifiable without a dedicated literature/archive audit.

why_this_matters: The strongest hidden-content signals are often not unusual names but broken or orphaned functional chains.
Reference-graph gaps can preserve implementation history that ordinary item lists miss.
Compiled test scripts can expose prototype mechanics even when the item has no normal acquisition route.
Duplicate helper forms can reveal abandoned revisions without requiring loose source assets.
research_value.generalized_datamining_pattern: SOURCE ESM -> RECORD IDENTITY -> INBOUND REFERENCES -> OUTBOUND FUNCTIONAL CHAIN -> SCRIPT SEMANTICS -> RUNTIME REACHABILITY -> PUBLIC FOOTPRINT -> CLAIM CEILING

targets: CONT containers with no ordinary placement
persistent references reachable only from scripts
cross-DLC revision ghosts and duplicated helper forms
next_gate.success_condition: Produce a machine-readable candidate table where each candidate records first missing runtime edge, surviving functional descendants, script behavior, and confidence-separated interpretation.

notes: This node is intentionally a datamining registry rather than a lore article. It preserves what the shipped data graph supports, keeps public novelty separate, and is designed to be extended as deeper orphan-reference audits are completed.
